Rules / Tool

SK9024 No solution or project could be loaded

The workspace load mode produced no compilation. Either nothing was found — no .slnx, .sln or .csproj under the root — or something was found and could not be opened: an explicit --project that does not exist, several candidates with none chosen, no MSBuild to be located, an assembly missing from the Skala installation, an exception from MSBuildWorkspace, or every project loading as a placeholder with zero documents. The same id also relays MSBuild's own workspace diagnostics verbatim, prefixed workspace:, at info or warning. Name the target with --project, or read a build with --load=binlog.

CategoryTool
Default severityerror
ScopeCompilation
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileno — it reads the whole compilation
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since0.6

Why

One id for the rung, because what the reader needs is which rung failed and why, and the message carries the why. The placeholder case exists because MSBuildWorkspace hands back a project with no documents rather than throwing, so a load that produced not one line of code was not empty, and the measured symptom was one failure diagnostic, one project, zero documents, zero findings, exit 0. Every outright failure marks the load failed, which stops the ladder when the caller named --load=workspace — or when auto chose it, which is verify, arrange and fix over any tree holding a project — and exits 4. Under the default --load=binlog ladder, where workspace is the middle rung, the ladder continues to loose with SK9025 and keeps this diagnostic at error severity, and the reliability gate fails the verdict on it at exit 1 (#361): the syntactic half is reported and is not allowed to pass as the whole.

When it does not fire

⚠ The relayed workspace: lines are MSBuild's text under this id and most of them are benign: this repository prints three Found project reference without a matching metadata reference lines on every workspace load, and they remain after a Debug build takes the run to zero findings — #336 was first misdiagnosed as their fault. Neither they nor the nothing-was-found case fail a run. A requested directory outside the repository root with no project of its own is refused rather than silently redirected to the root, and under --load=auto that refusal steers the load to loose instead.
